answers.reason: Sabta (H5454) is a Cushite name in GEN 10:7 and 1CH 1:9, also associated with a people or territory. None of the candidates represents that referent.
Sabtecha (H5455) is a Cushite name in GEN 10:7 and 1CH 1:9, also associated with a people or territory. None of the candidates represents that referent.
Sela-hammalekoth (H5555) is the rock or landmark near Maon where Saul stopped pursuing David in 1SA 23:28. None of the candidates is that location.
Ittah-kazin is an alternative spelling of Eth-kazin, the Zebulun boundary settlement in JOS 19:13. The candidate explicitly includes the label Ittah-kazin.
Padan is the shortened form of Paddan-aram used in GEN 48:7. Both records identify H6307, and the candidate includes Paddan as an alias.
Kirjath-arba is the former name of Hebron, explicitly identified in GEN 23:2 and JOS 14:15. The Hebron candidate includes Kiriath-arba and shares H7153.
Ramath of the south (H7418), also called Ramath-negeb, is mentioned in JOS 19:8. No candidates are supplied for a possible fold.
Shebah and Shiba are alternative renderings of the well named by Isaac in GEN 26:33. Both records identify H7656.
H8613 is the Tophet form used in ISA 30:33, a variant associated with Topheth in the Valley of Hinnom. The candidate already includes ISA 30:33 among its occurrences.
The record identifies a settlement at Merj Ekkeh, and none of the candidates identifies that settlement. Abilene in LUK 3:1 is a region, a separate geographic referent from a town named Abila.
